inputs.original_text: TAOISEACH Micheál Martin, speaking in Limerick this past week, said that housing tenancies have increased despite concern at a rise in eviction notices and homelessness in the wake of new rules, introduced by Government on March 1, forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants. The numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increased again [...] The post Taoiseach says housing tenancies have increased despite rise in eviction notices and homelessness appeared first on Limerick Post .
inputs.modified_text: The Taoiseach was in Limerick boasting that housing tenancies have risen even after his government imposed those March 1 rules forcing landlords into six-year leases. He waved off the clear spike in eviction notices and homelessness, but the numbers of people stuck in emergency accommodation have climbed again nationwide. This is the predictable result of heavy-handed government interference in private rental agreements that undermines property rights and family stability. We need to restore order through personal responsibility and market signals instead of letting bureaucrats erode the foundations of a stable society.
